patches: REPAIR 1 (common/scanner.h, scan_pi_content): the trailing `advance_if_eq(lexer, chr)` became `skip_if_eq`. `advance_if_eq` is defined as `if (!eof && lookahead==chr) advance(); else return false`, so its `else` ABORTED a token whose value the test could not affect — the statements run past `mark_end`, so they are pure lookahead. A processing instruction WITH CONTENT therefore produced no `_pi_content` token at all, the construct could not complete, and the parser wrapped it in an ERROR node; with no XMLDecl the enclosing `prolog` was destroyed too, taking any DOCTYPE in it. Isolated to the byte by a 19-shape battery: the construct parses iff the byte after `?>` is a newline.

REPAIR 2 (xml/grammar.js, _intSubset): `repeat(choice($._markupdecl, $.conditionalSect, $._DeclSep))` over a named `_intSubsetItem`, plus a `conditionalSect` rule. Upstream could not reach a conditional section from an internal subset at ANY version measured — 0.5.0-0.6.x declare `conditionalSect` in the `dtd` grammar and inline it, but `_intSubset` referenced `$._markupdecl`, which does not include it; 0.7.0 does not declare it in the `xml` grammar at all. The failure wrapped the `doctypedecl` in an ERROR, the parser took a LATER `Name` as the DTD's name, and the analyzer published a Type symbol literally called `INCLUDE`.
grammarPin.patchAdmissibility: 8,888 corpus files / 6.69M nodes, ERROR and MISSING counted per file: 31 files repaired, 2 moved, 8,855 unchanged, corpus MISSING nodes 32 -> 10. BOTH movements are adjudicated by measurement in fixtures/xml/out/regression-adjudication.json: one is a standalone `.dtd` (root ERROR under every build, so never in the wired surface; upstream's separate `dtd` grammar parses it with 0 ERROR nodes) and the other is libxml2's own fuzzer-regression directory, kept by the project precisely because those files must not parse.

internal_silent._rule: The gate has exactly FOUR buckets — handled_verified, internal_silent, gap, and a design_decision carrying a node_type — so `internal_silent` is the UNION of 'walked through with no output' and 'walked through to read a child'. A pass-through is a member of it. Derived from the analyzer's own PASSTHROUGH_LITERALS plus the hidden rules, so it cannot drift; the FIRST version of this file listed only the former and the gate reported `Mixed` and `children` as in NO bucket, which is the gate being right and this file being behind.

decisions.ruling: an element that ADOPTS a named reusable definition it does not declare — XSLT 2.
decisions.resolution: an element that ADOPTS a named reusable definition it does not declare — XSLT 2.0's `xsl:use-attribute-sets` (§10.6) or `xsl:use-package` (§12.1), the only two in any W3C XML vocabulary that do this. Probe: every element in the XSLT namespace whose local name is one of those two, counted on the parse tree with namespace resolution applied. MEASURED 0 occurrences across the 2,500-file family-stratified draw (86 distinct node types, 2,787,237 nodes, 110 repositories), so the ruling is not falsified by that draw. Instrument B and not A because the string-shaped population here is real and A cannot see it: XSD writes the WORD `use` as an ordinary attribute value (`<xs:attribute use="required">`), and a grammar inventory would be silent about that while a reader reasonably expects it to have been considered. That attribute is a CONSTRAINT keyword whose three values (`required`, `optional`, `prohibited`) name no construct in the document, so it is not a use of anything — but this lane did not MEASURE its corpus frequency, and that is recorded as a declared limitation rather than asserted either way. DECLINED as neighbours: `xsl:import` (already an `imports` edge carrying a file path), `xsl:key` (declares a named key that is then used, so the KEY is the declaration and a query is a `references` edge), and `xs:include`/`xs:import` in XSD (same file-path reasoning). OVERTURN: a non-zero count of either element name in the XSLT namespace on the parse tree.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.node_type: export_declaration / export_statement / export_list / module_export / export_spec / exported_item / public_declaration
decisions.ruling: a declaration that names what a document or module PUBLISHES.
decisions.resolution: a declaration that names what a document or module PUBLISHES. Instrument A, because an export in any W3C XML vocabulary would be an element in a published specification, and this grammar gives published elements their own node types: it produced 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw and NONE of the seven candidates above appears among them. Instrument A is UNSOUND for a construct written as ordinary syntax, and that exposure is real here, so the string-shaped population is measured and carried rather than assumed absent: 611 elements whose local name contains "export" across 3 files — 610 `<exports>` in `libxslt/doc/libxslt-api.xml`, `libxslt/doc/EXSLT/libexslt-api.xml` and `ghostty/DoxygenLayout.xml`, which are gtk-doc/Doxygen XML DESCRIBING the exported API of a C library and are documentation payload rather than an XML declaration, plus 1 `<exportedmodules>` in a Doxygen configuration file. The surface that would carry an `exports` edge already exists and is measured: every symbol a document publishes is reachable as a `contains` target, and `contains` resolves at BOTH ends on 100.0% of its 77,721 edges in the same draw. OVERTURN: any of the seven node types above at a non-zero count in the grammar inventory, or — independently, and as a search rather than a list of seven — any node type the grammar produces whose name contains `export` at a non-zero count over the corpus.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.ruling: a clause in which a declaration takes on the OBLIGATIONS of another type — an implements/extends clause, a superclass, an interface list.
decisions.resolution: a clause in which a declaration takes on the OBLIGATIONS of another type — an implements/extends clause, a superclass, an interface list. Instrument A: 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw, none of the five candidates above present. The nearest XML construct is XSD type DERIVATION (`<xs:extension base="T">` / `<xs:restriction base="T">`, XSD 1.0 Part 1 §3.4.2), and that is EMITTED as `extends` — 1,033 derivation sites over 95 files in this draw, 354 `extends` edges — because derivation names a base TYPE, which is the relation `extends` carries. What XML has no way to write is an obligation without a base: no element in any W3C XML vocabulary declares that its target satisfies another type's interface. The string-shaped population is measured and carried: 5 elements across 4 files — 2 `<interface>` in `ghostty/src/apprt/gtk/winproto/wayland/protocols/vicinae-hotkey-v1.xml`, which DECLARE a Wayland protocol interface rather than implement one, and 3 `<abstract>` in DocBook (`libxslt/doc/tutorial/libxslttutorial.xml`, `otp/lib/xmerl/doc/examples/xml/xmerl.xml`, `otp/lib/xmerl/doc/examples/xml/xmerl_xs.xml`), which are PROSE about an abstract class in a C++ manual. All five are generic `element` nodes in no vocabulary namespace, which is exactly why instrument A does not fire on them and a local-name probe would have. OVERTURN: any of the five node types above at a non-zero count, or an element in a vocabulary namespace whose defined semantics are interface satisfaction.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.ruling: an expression or element that CREATES an instance of a declared construct.
decisions.resolution: an expression or element that CREATES an instance of a declared construct. Instrument A: 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw, none of the five candidates above present, and the inventory contains no construction form of any kind — the 86 are prolog, element, attribute, content, DOCTYPE and its declarations, entity/notation declarations, conditional sections, PI, CDSect/CDATA and the anonymous punctuation tokens. Measured from the other side as well, because instrument A alone would be the json lane's mistake: 0 elements whose local name is new / instantiate / newinstance / create, across the same draw. The nearest XML constructs are an XSD `element` DECLARATION (which declares a type; it does not create a value) and an XSLT `xsl:element` / `xsl:copy-of` instruction (which create an output node from a name attribute, and the name is already a `references` edge) — in both cases the document names something rather than instantiating a declared type, which is the distinction this ruling rests on. OVERTURN: any of the five node types above at a non-zero count, or any node type the grammar produces whose name contains `new` or `instantiat` at a non-zero count over the corpus.

notApplicable.concept: calls / extends / overrides — NOT applicable, and this entry is the record of that being WRONG
notApplicable.measured: This entry previously claimed all four of `calls`, `extends`, `implements`, `overrides` and `instantiates` inapplicable, on the reasoning that an XSD names a type by an ATTRIBUTE VALUE so `base=` is a `references` edge. The M60 ontology census overturned it by measurement: `calls` is emitted for XSLT `xsl:call-template` (XSLT 1.0 §6, 548 edges), `extends` for XSD `<xs:extension base=>`/`<xs:restriction base=>` type derivation (XSD 1.0 §3.4.2, 438 edges), and `overrides` for XSLT 1.0 §5.5 competing template rules — that last one only after script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts reported this lane's RULED verdict FALSIFIED over 11,456 files (3 sites in 3 files, e.g. libxslt/tests/docbook/fo/toc.xsl lines 180 and 190). The reasoning was not wrong about the SYNTAX: `base=` is an attribute value. It was wrong about the RELATION, because a vocabulary element that defines a relation is a declaration of that relation however its operand is spelled. Kept as a record because a reader comparing this spec against an older one needs to see that the claim changed and why.

routed (`.dtd` is in EXTENSION_LANGUAGE) but NOT representable: the xml grammar's `document` rule requires a document element, so a standalone DTD's root node type is ERROR. Measured: `cond_sect1.dtd` 11 ERROR nodes, `cond_sect2.dtd` 8, the W3C `XMLSchema.dtd` 170 — while upstream's SEPARATE `dtd` grammar parses all of them with 0. Filed as owed, with its measurement, in grammars/tree-sitter-xml/PIN.md; the corpus files are declared negative controls rather than excluded by a glob.

kindRulings.contains: structural containment read straight off the tree: element->element, element->attribute, element->namespace, DTD->declaration, declaration->content-model member, declaration->notation, PI->target. Every contains TARGET is a published symbol in the same file — enforced structurally, not by convention, and pinned by `xml/dtd-declarations` (`every contains target resolves to a symbol in the same file`).
kindRulings.references: a NAME, never a written value. The target of an XSD/RelaxNG/XSLT reference is the LOCAL NAME and the prefix rides in metadata, because a prefix in a target is a value where a name belongs (M60.R10). An edge is emitted only when the target resolves in the document or is a specification built-in — 1,319 unresolved values are REFUSED rather than published.
kindRulings.imports: a FILE PATH, which is the one case where a value IS the right target: a DOCTYPE's ExternalID, a DTD entity's or notation's ExternalID, a StyleSheetPI/XmlModelPI `href`, and an XSD `schemaLocation` URI. 630 distinct schemaLocation targets and 11 external-ID imports were emitted where the pre-fix lane emitted 0.

line.note: every relationship carries a line, and 100% of them are on the line the TARGET NAME is written on (M59.A7 / #825). Pre-fix: the external-ID edge took the ExternalID node's line, so a multi-line PUBLIC doctype pointed at the keyword — 310 wrong-line edges, now 18. Pinned by all 8 fixtures, and by the multi-line doctype in `xml/dtd-declarations`, which is the shape that makes the keyword-line mutant non-vacuous.

occurrences.note: edge collapse is COUNTED, not hidden. Edge identity is `source|type|target`, so N declarations of one pair necessarily share one edge — 492,774 occurrences on 45,297 edges. The edge keeps the EARLIEST line the name is written on, not the first the LIFO walk reached. Pinned by `xml/edge-collapse`.

syntaxErrors.note: a symbol or edge from a file the analyzer reports as erroneous says so. Pre-fix: 27,228 symbols over 177 files, unlabelled, and the shipped 'creates no recovery symbols' check was a FIXTURE ACCIDENT. Suppressing them would be wrong (177 of 177 are `##` Maven-archetype templates), so they are labelled. Pinned by `xml/recovery-labelling`, including the negative half — a clean file carries no label, so the flag cannot become noise.

declaredName.note: in a declaration vocabulary the DECLARED name is an attribute VALUE, and the tag name is kept as `meta.tagName` so the structural reading is carried rather than overwritten. Gated on the element's EFFECTIVE NAMESPACE: 29,196 `name` attributes outside any declaration vocabulary are DATA and must not be renamed, which is why the rule is not tag-gated. Recall 0.045 -> 0.696 over 26,578 in-vocabulary declarations.

resolvable.note: a `references` edge records whether its target resolves `in-document` or is a specification `builtin`, so a consumer can tell a resolved edge from a built-in one without re-deriving the namespace bindings.
